gap.severity_rationale: Not P0: module, contract doc and transport pump all explicitly disclaim continuous proof, so nothing currently misrepresents a PASS. But clearance_violation -> rejected_clearance makes a PASS the operative 'clearance satisfied' signal used to commit a trajectory to the session, and the disclaimer is quantitatively load-bearing.

witness.construction: knot interval h=0.005 s; 203 alternating control points x in {0.85, 1.45}, y=0, z=2; duration ~1.0 s
witness.mechanism: curve x-period 2h = 0.010 s equals the default sample stride, so every sample lands on the curve peak (x=1.25) and the trough (x=1.05) falls exactly between samples

independent_continuous_scan.method: 400000-point dense scan of the continuous curve using scene_profile.segment_clearance

witness.reachability: Structurally valid bridge payload (order=3, len(knots)=len(pos_pts)+4, finite strictly-increasing knots, drone_id=0, empty yaw); the bridge imposes no amplitude or kinematic bound.

prototype_sound_certificate.basis: B-spline convex-hull property: on knot span [u_k, u_{k+1}) the curve lies in the convex hull of active control points P_{k-p}..P_k; their AABB is a sound outer bound.
prototype_sound_certificate.obstacle_rule: aabb_gap(control_bbox, obstacle) - vehicle_radius >= required_clearance for every span
prototype_sound_certificate.envelope_rule: every control point inside the inset map AABB
properties: conservative (will reject some genuinely safe curves; tightening via exact convex-hull-AABB distance or Bezier subdivision is a later, still no-native refinement)
no native, pure Python, directly testable
prototype_sound_certificate.note: Prototype lives only in check_g3_closure.py inside the audit directory; no shared code was modified.
